content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp are low‑calorie, high‑protein seafood. Combined with carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy vegetables (spinach, kale) the dish provides a wide range of vitamins, minerals and fiber. It is prepared without potatoes or sauce, making it light and nutritious.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp contain astaxanthin, a powerful antioxidant that gives them their pink hue.
Broccoli is one of the most nutrient‑dense vegetables, rich in vitamin C, K and folate.
Carrots are high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark‑green leafy greens such as spinach and kale supply iron, calcium and vitamin K.
Shrimp cook very quickly – usually 2‑3 minutes on a hot pan.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Shrimp provide complete protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The dish contains very little saturated fat, suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Shrimp are a good source of vitamin B12, essential for nerve function and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Broccoli and leafy greens are packed with vitamins C and E and flavonoids that combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots and lutein from leafy greens help maintain healthy vision.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to shrimp, ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Non‑organic vegetables may carry pesticide residues; thorough washing is recommended.

items.title: Fiber digestion
items.content: Large amounts of raw leafy greens can cause gas and bloating in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sauté shrimp over high heat for 2‑3 minutes until pink. Add sliced carrots and broccoli and cook another 4‑5 minutes, then stir in leafy greens and toss briefly until wilted. Season with salt, pepper and a squeeze of lemon if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh shrimp refrigerated and use within 2 days; cooked dish can be stored in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Store vegetables in the crisper drawer after rinsing.
